drone: Simulated drone concept: rockfall zone traced from imagery, not verified
eva: Backup shares 0 m with the main route
orbital: Candidate from orbit only: not crew clearance
rover: Simulated: rover stopped, wheel slip 38 percent, requesting input

sensor_evidence.thermal: simulated thermal camera: surface cooler than surroundings (possible loose material)

stages.text: From NASA orbital data only: drive the crew rover 0.9 km north across the crater floor to a parking spot above the scarp's low east end, then walk 832 m down to the viewpoint below the ice face. Slope comes from the HiRISE DTM; the scarp edge, foot and rockfall zone are traced from imagery (inferred). Rocks under 1 m, loose ground and shadow are not assessed.
stages.title: Orbital planning

stages.text: The day before the walk, the simulated rover drives the candidate route. About 0.4 km out it reports soft ground the orbit could not see (simulated) and stops; the drive is replanned around it (+13 m).
stages.title: Rover reconnaissance

stages.text: The simulated drone images the scarp face from the pit floor and checks the ground around the viewpoints. The rockfall zone shown is the traced-foot rule, not something the drone measured.
stages.title: Drone inspection

stages.text: Review the replanned route two astronauts would take to the viewpoint, the evidence behind it and the backup. Budgets use pipeline.itinerary with 5,000 m rule on walking distance only (team decision 2026-11-14). None of this is crew clearance.
stages.title: Astronaut mission review
